Subject: Sprint Zero intake — CrystalTek on-prem K8s: inventory, node pools, storage questions

Hi Rajiv / Tom,

Thanks again for the kickoff this week — good coverage on regulatory needs. Per our conversation, I’m opening a short intake thread to capture the minimum fields we need to size and propose a Sprint Zero for your on-prem Kubernetes deployment (Cluster A / primary site).

Could you please return the attached site inventory (one line per rack/room) with these fields filled where available:
- Rack/room name
- Number of servers (CPU/GPU type)
- Local disk types / sizes (NVMe / SATA / iSCSI)
- Network uplink capacity and redundant switches
- Power redundancy (A/B PDU)
- Rack-level temperature constraints or scheduled maintenance windows

We’ll use this to:
- Propose node pool sizing (control plane, infra, GPU worker slices, burst pool)
- Map PV class recommendations (ephemeral SSD, encrypted blockstore, archival)
- Draft an initial runbook for cutover and evacuation procedures

Attachment: crystaltek-site-a-inventory.csv (template)

Target turnaround: end of next week (May 14). If some info is sensitive, feel free to mark fields “redacted” and we’ll coordinate a secure upload to your SFTP / our private intake endpoint.

Cheers,

Camila Reyes

Camila — thanks, attaching a filled inventory for Site A. I answered inline where we had quick clarifications. A few callouts:

- We have a mix of 8 x A100-GPU servers and 24 x CPU-only hosts across two racks (Rack A1/A2).
- Local NVMe on GPU hosts: 2 x 3.2TB per host; CPU hosts have 1 x 1.6TB NVMe + 2 x 4TB SATA for archival.
- Network: 25Gb leaf uplinks to leaf-spine with redundant paths; egress through a shared border with IPSEC to cloud partner.
- Power: dual A/B PDUs on both racks.
- Retention/regulatory: audit logs (write-once) must be kept on an encrypted blockstore for 2 years.

Questions from our side:
1) Do you recommend HSM integration for key wrapping for the encrypted blockstore or will KMS suffice?
2) For models with large KV caches (3–6GB per worker), can Redwood put a hard cap on RAM per container to keep eviction predictable?

I’ve attached site-inventory-completed.csv.

Thanks Camila — sketched a proposal and quick MVP checklist below. Attaching a short M.A.P (mutual action plan) PDF.

High-level node-pool proposal (Site A):
- control-plane: 3 x dedicated small VMs (non-GPU), colocated across A1/A2 with anti-affinity, managed as static pods for etcd and control components.
- infra pool: 4 x CPU hosts for sidecars (routing, logging, metrics) with ephemeral NVMe for buffers.
- gpu-worker-slice: 6 x A100 (8 GPU hosts split into primary pool) pinned to large-GPU node taints for steady throughput.
- burst-gpu-pool: 2 x A100 spare nodes for sudden peak and experiments; autoscaling via our burst policy (max 50% of primary pool).

Storage mapping recommendations:
- ephemeral SSD class (fast local NVMe) for KV cache and per-request temp storage (no backups).
- encrypted-blockstore (network-attached, LUKS+KMS) for audit logs — mount with read-once policy; backup to archival.
- archival SATA pool for long-term storage | offline cold tier (backup snapshots encrypted).

HSM vs KMS:
- Recommendation: KMS with key-wrapping supported by customer HSM for highest assurance. We can support KMS-only for lower friction, but if CrystalTek requires FIPS/HSM-attested keys, we’ll include HSM integration as a workstream (estimated +2 weeks ops + a runbook).

KV cache memory caps:
- Redwood runtime supports per-container memory limits via the operator; we propose a hard cap at 12GB per replica for models with 3–6GB KV usage so eviction is predictable. We’ll include a monitoring policy to surface cache pressure and automated fallback to the burst pool.

M.A.P attachments: sprint-zero-mavplan.pdf (contains sprint milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria).

Next steps:
1) Camila / Karthik to confirm HSM path;
2) Rajiv to sign off on node counts or propose tradeoffs;
3) Schedule a 60-min architecture review (tech working session) — suggested Wed May 12 10:00–11:00 PT.

—Priya

Rajiv / Tom — attaching a short mutual action plan and the proposed node-pool + storage mapping for Site A based on the inventory you provided. Highlights & ask:

- We recommend moving forward with KMS + optional HSM; if you need FIPS-backed HSM we’ll scope an HSM integration sprint (+2 weeks ops). Please reply with preference.
- Node counts: primary GPU pool = 6 hosts; burst = 2 spare hosts. Please confirm OK to reserve 8 hosts for Redwood workloads (we will not consume full GPU vCPU capacity permanently).
- Acceptance criteria for Sprint Zero: control-plane HA verified, PV classes provisioned and encryption validated, successful end-to-end inference smoke test using a 2B-parameter model within target latency bounds.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm HSM vs KMS by EOD Wed May 12.
2) Sign the M.A.P (attached) to kick off procurement and on-site access scheduling.
3) Tech working session Wed May 12 10:00 PT — please confirm attendee list.

Thanks and excited to get started — ping me here or via Slack for quick clarifications.
